dimensions.assessment: Affects motor vehicle manufacturers, vehicle owners and operators, first responders, and consumers through recalls, safety ratings, and educational programs.
dimensions.evidence: establish a voluntary process under which a manufacturer may test the performance of passenger motor vehicles

dimensions.assessment: Changes vehicle exemption caps from 2,500 to 90,000 vehicles, alters recall notification procedures, and establishes new administrative offices.
Requires numerous administrative studies, reports, and advisory groups without specifying large direct federal appropriations.
dimensions.evidence: The Administrator shall conduct a study to identify factors that result in a motor vehicle involved in a recall not receiving the service

dimensions.assessment: Amends multiple titles of U.S. Code regarding motor vehicle safety, standardizes rulemaking priorities, and establishes new working groups and offices.
dimensions.evidence: establish an office within the Administration to be known as the Office of the New Car Assessment Program

dimensions.assessment: Implements permanent procedural changes, recurring multi-year reviews, and advisory committees with defined termination timelines.
dimensions.evidence: Not later than 1 year after the date of the enactment of this Act, and every 4 years thereafter, the Administrator shall conduct a review

importance_detail.rationale: Reforms the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration's safety programs, establishes new offices and advisory committees, changes vehicle exemption limits, and orders multiple comprehensive studies.
